name: Cauliflower

evidence.quote: The brassica family is quite cold resistant, making them well adapted to cool season production. ... Young, hardened cauliflower plants can withstand temperatures of 0 °C for less than 36 hours. The minimum and maximum growing temperatures for cauliflower are 0 and 30 °C, with the optimum growing temperature for this crop between 15 and 22 °C.
evidence.doc: Production Guidelines for Cauliflower, DAFF (South Africa), n.d.

frostTender.notes: Not a frost-killed warm-season crop, so the catalog's 'frost-tender' gate does not apply — but it is also not fully frost-hardy like cabbage: KZN DARD's Cole Crops chapter warns 'Mature curds, if not protected by leaves, can be easily damaged by only a few degrees of frost. Heavy frosts can cause serious damage to the crop' (kzndard.gov.za, Cole Crops, p.2). Curd protection near frost season is a real farmer-facing caveat even though value=false.

seedRateNotes: DAFF: 'Normally 300 g of seed will produce enough plants for one hectare' (transplants) vs 'When direct seeding, 1 kg of seed is required per hectare' (p.11-12). KZN's 120-200g (seedtray) / 250-500g (seedbed) figures are per-hectare-of-transplants seedbed quantities, not a field broadcast rate, so no single seedRateKgPerHaRange is recorded — the two DAFF figures (0.3kg/ha via transplants, 1kg/ha direct-seeded) are kept as prose rather than merged into a misleading range.

varietiesNotes: Zone assignments above are this research pass's placement of DAFF's quoted 'Season' values (Summer/Winter/Year round/etc.) onto the catalog's 8 SA growing zones — neither DAFF nor KZN DARD map these cultivars to named zones directly, so treat zones as a reasonable inference, not a sourced claim, distinct from the directly-quoted days-to-maturity and season text.

zoneNotes.highveld: Cool-season crop matches this zone's climate; DAFF's Cold-areas/heavy-frost sowing window (Aug-Sep, Dec-Mar) applies, but curds need leaf protection against heavy frost near maturity (KZN DARD, Cole Crops, p.2).
zoneNotes.lowveld-bushveld: DAFF: cauliflower 'will also seldom give an acceptable yield or quality if it matures during hotter weather' (Cole Crops p.2) — workable with careful season timing (winter window) rather than as a summer crop.
zoneNotes.subtropical-coast: KZN DARD's 'Hot areas / Frost-free' sowing window (Feb-Apr) applies; several 'Year round' cultivars (Huntsmen, Juneau, TSX C22, White Gold) are suited here.
zoneNotes.midlands-mistbelt: KZN DARD's own 'Cole Crops' chapter is written primarily for this zone; most named KZN cultivars (Incline, Glacier, Arizona, etc.) and the moderate-frost sowing window apply directly.
zoneNotes.western-cape: Not covered by a Western-Cape-specific source in this pass; DAFF's Autumn/Winter/Spring cultivars (Lagardo, Arano) fit a winter-rainfall cool season by inference only — flagged as a gap.
zoneNotes.southern-cape: Same gap as western-cape — no Southern Cape-specific source found; winter/autumn cultivars inferred to fit this all-year-rainfall mild coast.
zoneNotes.karoo-arid: DAFF's 0-30°C growing range and poor performance in hot weather make this zone's extreme heat and aridity a poor fit; not listed as a production area by either source.
zoneNotes.high-mountain: Not addressed by source; DAFF/KZN DARD both warn that heavy frost damages unprotected mature curds, which is a concern in a severe-frost zone even though the plant itself is cold-tolerant.

gaps: No Western Cape / Southern Cape-specific sowing calendar found — the sourced 3-tier sowing table (Cold/Warm/Hot areas) is a summer-rainfall-oriented national/KZN table, not a winter-rainfall-specific one; 'winter' sowMonths are set equal to 'summer' by inference, following this catalog's cabbage/broccoli precedent, not a direct quote.
No EcoCrop row specific to Brassica oleracea var. botrytis was used (left null) rather than substituting a different cultivar-group's climate envelope.

Arano's DAFF table entry prints '90-20' for days-to-maturity — very likely an OCR/scan artefact of '90-120' (its head-mass, colour and use match the neighbouring rows) but recorded with that caveat rather than silently 'corrected'.
Named KZN cultivars (Incline, Glacier, Arizona, Fremont, Siria, Star 4403/4405, Tenere) have no individual season, maturity or zone data in the source beyond 'popular in KwaZulu-Natal'.
No single seedRateKgPerHaRange recorded — DAFF gives two different figures (0.3 kg/ha via transplants, 1 kg/ha direct-seeded) that describe different establishment methods rather than a single range.
summary: Sourced from DAFF's Cauliflower production guideline plus four KZN DARD 'Vegetable Production Guidelines' chapters (Plant Establishment, Cole Crops, Expected Yields, Length of Growing Period). SowMonths (summer/mild-frost/all-year), row/in-row spacing, sow depth, days-to-harvest (60-130d from transplant) and yield (7-20 t/ha, conservative-to-target) are all directly quoted, and eight named SA seed-trade cultivars span early-to-late maturity. The main gap is a Western Cape/Southern Cape-specific sowing calendar — the sourced 3-tier table is frost-severity-based rather than rainfall-pattern-based, so 'winter' is inferred equal to 'summer' rather than independently sourced.
